prompt: Rotation. Rotation is the movement of the Earth around its own axis is called Rotation. The earth rotates from west to east. It completes one full rotation in 24 hours. The speed of rotation is faster at the equator and slower at the poles. The axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5°. As the Earth is spherical in shape, only one half of the Earth receives sunlight at a time. Thus, the side of the Earth facing the Sun experience day. On the other hand, the other half, or the part away from the sun, experiences night. As the Earth rotates, the lighted part moves into the darkness. Rotation causes day and night.
